text:
Sam (Support): Hey team, customer reported a big billing spike tied to embeddings dashboard. They say the chart is labelled 'tokens' but numbers line up exactly with vector counts and look doubled. Customer: AcmeHealth (org_912). Request IDs attached. Escalating :warning:

Emma L.: Can you paste the org id + one request_id and a screenshot of the chart? Also which date range?

Sam (Support): Org: org_912. Example req: rq_20240315_8ab3. Date range: 2024-03-15 00:00 - 23:59 UTC. Screenshot: (uploaded). The customer says API logs show 10k vectors but dashboard shows 40k 'token' units.

Liam K.: @Sam thx. Initial guess: either unit label is wrong (vector vs token) OR the ingestion pipeline is duplicating rows before aggregation. Did they use batch embeddings?

Sam (Support): They do batch 50 per request. I included a curl from their app: `curl -X POST /v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1","inputs":[...50 items...]}' -H "Authorization: Bearer ..."`

Mike H.: Quick check — dashboard pipeline used to ingest per-item metrics when batch splitting was off. We shipped batch-split change last month to produce per-request and per-item events; if the dedupe key didn't get updated we could be summing both.

Julia R.: Can you share the raw metric rows? If we have two events per item (one from request-level and one from item-level) the visualization that sums `embedding_units` across both will double-count.

Sam (Support): Pasted minimal repro query they ran in Console analytics: 
```
SELECT date_trunc('hour', ts) as hour, sum(embedding_units) as units
FROM embeddings_metrics
WHERE org_id='org_912' AND ts >= '2024-03-15'
GROUP BY hour
ORDER BY hour;
```
They attached CSV — for 03:00 hour API log shows 10,200 vectors; dashboard returns 40,800 units.

metrics-bot: [ingest-alert] high-ingest-rate detected for org_912 at 2024-03-15T03:07:12Z :eyes:

Liam K.: That matches batch split + duplicate event ingestion. Two possible flows: (A) worker emitted per-request metric and later expanded to per-item with same request_id but different event_id and our dedupe used event_id only; (B) aggregation uses a faulty join across shards that multiplies rows. I'll investigate ingestion logs.

Mike H.: I pulled a sample of the raw events for rq_20240315_8ab3: we have 1 request-level row with embedding_units=50 and 50 item-level rows each with embedding_units=1 (this is an example normalized unit). The UI query currently SUMs everything, no de-duping. That explains approximate 51x counts for a single request. But customer's multiplier is 4x, so maybe their unit conversion (vector->token) in UI also multiplies by avg_dims (e.g., 768) incorrectly. Need to confirm units: our billing uses 'vector-units' which is 1 per vector; legacy charts displayed 'token-units' (tokens) so label mismatch possible.

Julia R.: Repro steps for eng: 1) run the customer's batch request id above in staging with batch-split enabled, 2) query embeddings_metrics, 3) compare sum over event_type IN ('request','item') with dedupe on request_id.

Sam (Support): Customer asked for immediate correction — they got charged for the inflated numbers. How fast can we provide a corrected report and rollback?

Liam K.: Short-term: provide a corrected CSV by running the analytics query with `GROUP BY request_id` and dedupe. Example: 
```
SELECT request_id, sum(embedding_units) as units
FROM embeddings_metrics
WHERE org_id='org_912' AND ts BETWEEN '2024-03-15' AND '2024-03-15 23:59'
GROUP BY request_id;
```
This will count per-request once. I'll run that now and DM the CSV.

Mike H.: Longer-term: update the metrics pipeline to tag events as `granularity= request|item` and change UI default to collapse item-level into request-level for billing charts. Also fix chart label to 'vectors' when appropriate.

Julia R.: Adding to eng-runtime backlog and will do a quick triage. Assigning to @Liam K. for immediate fix and @Mike H. to own rollout.

Sam (Support): Sending customer interim corrected numbers and refund plan. I'll attach the corrected CSV when @Liam posts it. Thanks. :thumbsup:
